properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 24 at 4:07PM MDT until August 24 at 11:00PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Kane County in southern Utah...

* Until 1100 PM MDT Monday.

* At 407 PM MDT, the public reported high flows on upper reaches of
the Paria River south of Tropic. This flood wave will continue to
move downstream past Highway 89 and into the Lower Paria River
Canyon. Up to 2 inches of rain have fallen over the upper reaches
of the Paria River drainage. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Public reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks, streams, slot
canyons, and normally dry washes.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Areas along the Paria River in South Central Kane County, including
the Lower Paria River Canyon.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain. Dry
washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 11:00 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 11:00 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...
Illinois...

Wabash River from Montezuma to Mount Carmel

White River from Elliston to Hazleton

.Minor flooding continues along portions of central Indiana rivers
due to excessive rain over the previous few weeks. Largely dry
weather is in store for the week ahead, with only a few low chances
of rain.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River at Mount Carmel.

* WHEN...Until Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, River is bankfull in all locations.  All
oil field production ceases with the exception of pumping units on
substructures.  Access to these are by boat only.  Agricultural
losses increase dramatically.  Farmers move livestock to higher
ground.  City of Mount Carmel leaves flood gates B and C in year
round.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:45 AM CDT /12:45 PM EDT/ Monday the stage was 19.3 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:45 AM CDT /12:45 PM EDT/ Monday was 19.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 20.1 feet
early Thursday morning. It will then fall below flood stage early
Saturday morning.
- Flood stage is 19.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 130 AM CDT /230 AM
EDT/.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 24 at 3:15PM MDT until August 24 at 6:15PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Lee and P-L Gulch burn scars in...
Central Rio Blanco County in northwestern Colorado...

* Until 615 PM MDT.

* At 315 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Lee and P-L Gulch Burn Scars. Between 0.1 and
0.3 inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to
3 inches in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scars will result in
debris flow. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation
and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Lee and P-L Gulch Burn
Scars.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Lee and P-L Gulch Burn Scars.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Central Rio Blanco County.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Lee and P-L Gulch Burn Scars. Severe debris flows can also be
anticipated across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in
places. If you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of
creeks, roads and normally dry arroyos is likely. The heavy rains
will likely trigger rockslides, mudslides and debris flows in steep
terrain, especially in and around these areas.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.
